bubbleNote.blurb: Alabama sits at the 13 seed, one spot from being inside the field — the closest of the four bubble teams. The Tide are essentially one result from bracket position.
LSU holds the 14 seed, two spots outside the field, and draws No. 23 Clemson next. Beating a ranked team in Week 1 is exactly the kind of push a team on the bubble needs.
USC checks in at the 15 seed, three spots from the field. The Trojans have ground to make up and no cushion to lose.
BYU is the last team on the board at the 16 seed, four spots outside the field. The Cougars are hanging on and will need help — or a signature win — to climb.

games.blurb: No. 13 LSU opens as a 10.5-point favorite over No. 23 Clemson in Baton Rouge, with a 50.5 total pointing to a defensive night. A top-25 win in Week 1 is the kind of résumé line either side can lean on all season.
The Apple Cup returns with No. 19 Washington installed as a 21.5-point favorite at home. Rivalry math says close, the number says otherwise, and the Huskies can't afford a slip in their opener.

No. 10 Ole Miss is only a 6.5-point favorite against Louisville, a modest number for a top-10 team hosting a non-conference opponent. With the total at 55.5, the Rebels may need to trade scores to get out of Week 1 clean.
No. 5 Notre Dame hosts Wisconsin as a 20.5-point favorite with the total sitting at just 47.5. The Irish are expected to win big and win ugly, and anything less will get picked apart.
The Border War kicks off the season with Colorado State favored by four at home. A four-point line in a rivalry game is another way of saying nobody has any idea.
No. 16 Michigan is a 26.5-point favorite over Western Michigan in the opener. The scoreboard isn't the story here; how the Wolverines look while covering is.

predictions.blurb: Texas checks in at No. 4 in the poll while FPI slots the Longhorns second, meaning the metrics see a team with a real claim to being the best in the country. In the SEC, they'll get every chance to prove it.
Texas Tech sits 12th in the rankings with FPI a touch higher at No. 10 — the model likes the Red Raiders as a legitimate Big 12 front-runner rather than a fringe top-15 team.
Michigan is ranked 16th and FPI has the Wolverines 15th, about as close to consensus as it gets. Nobody's overrating them; nobody's writing them off either.
BYU is 15th in the poll but only 20th in FPI, the widest skepticism gap of the group. The Cougars will need Big 12 results to keep the ranking from drifting toward the model's number.
LSU opens 13th while FPI sees a top-10 team at No. 9. If the metrics are right, the Tigers are undervalued heading into a September that starts with Clemson.

fieldStorylines.blurb: Ohio State and Oregon are ranked first and second, separated by a single spot in the chase for the Big Ten's automatic bid. One stumble by the Buckeyes and the Ducks take the league lead outright.

Georgia leads the SEC race at No. 3 with Texas one rung behind at No. 4 — the tightest possible margin for a league whose auto bid may decide seeding at the top of the field. Neither has any room to give one away.
Texas Tech holds the Big 12's automatic bid position at No. 12 with BYU three spots back at No. 15. It's a workable cushion, but a single head-to-head-adjacent result could erase it.
